newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish TPSA bourses entry seen June or Sept 1998. [CORRECTED 12:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Polish TPSA bourses entry seen June or Sept 1998. [CORRECTED 12:15 GMT]

text.p: Polish state-owned telecoms giant Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) could enter the Warsaw bourse and foreign exchanges in June or September next year, the telecommunications minister said on Thursday.

The government's sell-off plan assumes that TPSA would be privatised in stages, with the first next year involving a public offering of about 25 percent of shares for both institutional and retail investors, in Poland and abroad.

"We expect shares of the company (TPSA) will be sold on domestic and foreign exchanges to individuals and institutions next year...we think it will be either June or September," Andrzej Zielinski told a news conference.
Zielinski said the treasury minister was obliged to present a plan of the sale by the end of next month.

According to the government plan, after the first stage the state treasury would retain control over the company with up to 15 percent of TPSA shares set aside for its employees and the public offer capped at 25 percent.
The plan does not rule out that the offer of existing shares could be combined with a capital increase.
The government had yet to decide the exact size of the public offer and how the shares would be divided between the domestic and foreign tranches.
The second stage of privatisation might involve finding a strategic investor but final decisions are to be made by the cabinet in cooperation with a privatisation adviser Poland has yet to appoint.
